messages:
maria: Heads up — ap-southeast1 GPUs: ~40 pods evicted over last 20m. Kube shows preemptions + OOM-like evictions but nodes look healthy. :warning:
jun: any patterns? same nodes/az?
maria: Mostly ap-southeast1-b. Scheduler complains about 'insufficient nics' for gang pods. Excerpt: FailedScheduling: 0/24 nodes are available: 12 Insufficient nics, 8 node(s) didn't match Pod's nodeAffinity.
chris: Insufficient nics? we don't advertise NIC count as a resource normally. Could be conntrack exhaustion from warm pool attach/detach bursts? :thinking:
ian: saw NIC flaps during a warm pool scale earlier. kube-proxy logs had: `conntrack: table full` on a few nodes — that causes kubelet to mark Unready briefly and triggers evictions.
jun: can you paste `sysctl -n net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` from an affected node?
maria: grabbed from gpu-apse1-12: `65536`. conntrack entries at peak: `64320`. so it's nearly full. also `kubectl describe node` showed NetworkUnavailable on a couple nodes.
chris: short-term fixes: bump conntrack_max or tune conntrack timeouts, but we should reduce attach/detach churn. which jobs were hot?
ian: recent scale events: batch-infer-spot, docs-embedder, canary-bench. batch-infer spins up many short-lived sidecars that open lots of ephemeral connections. we should add egress pooling/keepalives.
maria: proposal: manual sysctl bump on affected nodes to 200k and restart kube-proxy. anyone take the playbook?
jun: @chris i'll run the sysctl change on 6 nodes in ap-southeast1-b with lowest load, rolling 2 at a time.
chris: +1. also please open an infra ticket for config change + follow-up RFC. consider a scheduler taint when conntrack > 90% so we avoid packing more bursty pods there.
ian: i'll add a metric + alert on `conntrack_usage_percent` and a Cesium dashboard: trigger if avg over 5m > 85% -> page oncall.
sre-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-514 ap-southeast1 conntrack spike -> assigned to eng-infra
maria: Postmortem note: this wasn't classic GPU fragmentation — it's a NIC/conntrack-induced packing gap. important distinction for binpacking heuristics.
jun: action items: (1) Jun bump sysctl on 6 nodes (in progress), (2) Ian create alert + dashboard, (3) Chris open infra RFC for conntrack/scheduler policy, (4) Maria assemble affected customer list. updating thread as things progress.
chris: if bump works we can roll to other AZs, but app-level pooling is the long-term fix.
